newsitem.title: USA: Congress to address forex law tangle next year.
newsitem.headline: Congress to address forex law tangle next year.

text.p: A Senate bill to reform U.S. laws governing futures, expected to be reintroduced early next year, will likely include a provision to address a nettlesome foreign exchange trading controversy, a spokesman for the Senate Agriculture Committee said.
A version of the bill introduced this month by Senator Richard Lugar, chairman of the committee, and Patrick Leahy, the ranking Democrat, did not address the forex issue.
"We'll probably have Treasury Amendment language when we reintroduce the bill in the next Congress," said Senate Agriculture Committee spokesman Andy Fischer.
The 1974 Treasury Amendment to the Commodity Exchange Act was intended to exempt the interbank foreign exchange market from oversight by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.
But ambiguities have arisen concerning the scope of the amendment and the Supreme Court will hear a case on the issue next term.

Fischer denied a report in the Wall Street Journal on Friday that the Senators would wait until after the Supreme Court delivers a ruling on the current Treasury amendment, which is not expected to be handed down until next summer.
"I doubt that that is the case," Fischer said.
Lugar, an Indiana Republican, and Leahy, a Vermont Democrat, had hoped to address the forex problem in the bill they introduced this year.
But the CFTC and the Treasury Department were unable to reach a consensus recommendation over the summer on language for such a provision.

Lugar and Leahy had asked for a recommendation by September, but officials at the two agencies recently told the committee they needed more time. A recommendation could come at the end of the year, agency officials said.
